title: Pwyll and the Otherworld
subtitle: A prince swaps places with a deathless lord for a year — the opening of the Mabinogion

learningObjectives.text: What bargain does Arawn offer Pwyll?

main.author: various Welsh traditions
main.locator: The First Branch, Arawn asks Pwyll to defeat Hafgan; local text normalized characters 368527-368896
main.excerpt: One year from this night,” he answered, “is the time fixed between him and me that we should meet at the Ford; be thou there in my likeness, and with one stroke that thou givest him, he shall no longer live. And if he ask thee to give him another, give it not, how much soever he may entreat thee, for when I did so, he fought with me next day as well as ever before.”

narrativeBlocks.title: A hunt that opens a door
narrativeBlocks.body: Pwyll, prince of Dyfed, hunts on a misty morning and chases a strange stag — into a clearing where he meets Arawn, lord of Annwn, the Otherworld. They have offended each other's courtesy.

narrativeBlocks.title: The strangest bargain in Welsh myth
narrativeBlocks.body: Arawn offers a fix: swap places for one year. Pwyll will rule Annwn in Arawn's shape, fight Arawn's enemy king, and — the catch — share Arawn's queen's bed. Honour demands he touch no one.

narrativeBlocks.title: A year well kept
narrativeBlocks.body: Pwyll keeps the bargain perfectly: he defeats the enemy in the year-end single combat, and through a whole year in the Otherworld never touches the queen. Returning home, the two kingdoms are bound in friendship.

narrativeBlocks.title: Then comes Rhiannon
narrativeBlocks.body: The story's second wonder: Rhiannon rides past on a horse no rider can catch — until Pwyll simply asks her to stop. She has come for him, having refused the suitor her father chose. The marriage is made with her consent, not the suitor's claim.

narrativeBlocks.title: What the tale is for
narrativeBlocks.body: The Mabinogion's first branch teaches the book's values: a bargain kept, a woman choosing her own husband, the Otherworld a mirror to the courtly one. These tales care about honour more than swordplay.

quiz.prompt: What is Arawn's bargain with Pwyll?

choices.text: Foster his son for seven years
Swap places for a year — rule Annwn, fight his enemy, and share his queen's bed without touching her

quiz.explanation: The year-long exchange tests courtesy above all — Pwyll keeps it perfectly.

choices.text: She chooses Pwyll herself — riding past uncatchably until he simply asks her to stop, refusing the suitor chosen for her
She is won in a tournament
Her father offers her as a prize

quiz.explanation: Her agency is the point — the tale gives her the choosing.
